summary.intent: Avoid reloading root CA certificates on every HTTPS request with verify=True, which profiling showed spends most wall-clock time in urllib3/OpenSSL's load_verify_locations() and materially hurts concurrent throughput; cache a single default-CA-bundle SSLContext once at import and reuse it for every default-trust-store request instead of triggering that call per request.
summary.issue_fit: No originating issue is linked; intent is taken from the user-supplied PR title/body (spec-pr-6667) and the four real commit messages. All four commit-level promises and the PR's core acceptance goal are met by the diff.
summary.coverage: The single changed file (src/requests/adapters.py, +28/-18) was read in full function context at base and head; no other files changed. Ran the 8 focused SSL/cert-related tests offline at the reviewed head (5 passed, 3 failed; all three failures are pre-existing/environmental, not introduced here). Because the change touches the TLS-verification/concurrency risk area, dispatched one fresh-context verifier batch against three safety premises (shared-context thread-safety, verification strength, connection-pool key separation); all three ruled `holds`.
check_details: Reviewer ran `PYTHONPATH=<clone>/src <cache>/venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_requests.py -k "cert_verify or ca_certificate or ca_cert_bundles or ssl_certificate_files or http_with_certificate or different_connection_pool_for_tls or different_connection_pool_for_mtls or pyopenssl_redirect"` at head 4089f3dc65f783beaa53cc032958ab625440d0ac: 5 passed, 3 failed, 321 deselected.

test_pyopenssl_redirect and test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert fail with `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: ... Missing Authority Key Identifier`, a stale test-fixture-certificate mismatch under the installed OpenSSL that the run policy documents as pre-existing at both base and head.

test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings fails on its very first call (verify=False) with a CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED alert; that call only exercises the verify=False branch of cert_verify()/_urllib3_request_context(), which this diff leaves byte-for-byte unchanged, so the failure cannot be attributed to this change; the verifier's own independent run corroborates the sibling test's same root cause.

Dispatched a fresh-context verifier (bundle d11218eff36970e37ccc8a3a3bc6e2e4) for 3 safety premises about the shared `_preloaded_ssl_context` (thread-safety of reuse across concurrent handshakes, verification strength vs. the pre-change per-request context, and connection-pool cache-key separation between verify=True/False/str); all three ruled `holds`, citing urllib3's connection.py and poolmanager.py sources plus one focused test it re-ran itself.

observations.fact: Loading the default CA bundle now happens once at import of `requests.adapters` rather than lazily on the first verify=True HTTPS request, so an unreadable default bundle would surface as an import-time exception instead of the previous per-request `OSError` (a related zip/pyinstaller-extraction concern was already raised and resolved during review by moving the extraction to this same call site).
observations.evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:75-78; PR conversation comment by sigmavirus24: "Ah, I see that the PR was updated and moved the extraction."

tasks.premise: The module-level `_preloaded_ssl_context`, created once and never reconfigured to a divergent value afterward, is safe to share concurrently across simultaneous TLS handshakes to different hosts.
The shared `_preloaded_ssl_context` enforces the same CERT_REQUIRED/check_hostname=True validation as the pre-change per-request context; verify=True is not silently weakened.
urllib3's PoolManager keys cached HTTPSConnectionPools on ssl_context/ca_certs/ca_cert_dir/cert_reqs, so a verify=True pool is never reused as a verify=False or verify=<path> pool, or vice versa.
